claims.text: stakeholder-update-example.md lines 3-4: one plan (refund-plan-example.md), each party needs a different part; the table was made at Sprint 15 planning and is reviewed with the risk register.
Lines 8-14: five stakeholders (customer care, accounting, gateway provider, product owner, operations) with columns: what they care about, what the team needs from them, when/how they hear.

Table rows: customer care wants to know when self-service refunds come, to cut calls; team needs a person for refused refunds and common questions; hears by short email after each sprint review and at once when the forecast changes. Accounting: list format before end of Sprint 15.
Gateway provider row: technical email when needed; operations row: via the product owner, before Sprint 16.

Update lines 18-34: forecast week 8 to week 10 from now, a range not a date, will tell when it changes; risk: the gateway connection never done, trying it this week; two requests before end of next week; meanwhile refund calls handled as today.

Lines 36-38: the update has no 'sprint', 'story point' or 'velocity' because the reader does not use those words; if the forecast changes after the week with the gateway, the team sends a new update the same day, not waiting until week 8.
Week 8 to week 10 matches the forecast of 4 to 5 two-week sprints from the start of Sprint 15 in velocity-history.md.

Stakeholders include people outside the team; each cares about a different part of one plan; an update gives range, risks and requests in the reader's words; they hear of a change as soon as the team knows. Anyone may draft an update.

risk-register-example.md line 12 (R2): the developer doing the integration owns R2, asking the gateway's provider in week one about an idempotency key; stakeholder table: operations is reached via the product owner (scope question).
